course: 1C:Enterprise 8 Programming — from foundations to professional development
module: Platform architecture, infobases and development environments
title: Your training infobase: create, open and preserve a copy
goal: Prepare your own infobase and verify a separate restoration.

prerequisites.text: Distinguish platform, configuration and data from the preceding lesson.

sections.title: A directory and a startup entry are different
paragraphs: A file infobase resides in its chosen directory. A startup-list entry opens that location; the entry is not a backup. Renaming it does not move database contents. Removing an entry and deleting files also differ, so this lesson deletes neither. Choose a new directory whose purpose is clear, such as your personal training service desk.

Give copies explicit purposes: primary training, change experiment and restored check. Designer titles can show the same configuration name. Before restoration verify the selected startup entry and directory, not only the title.

sections.title: Choose by content
paragraphs: A project name does not mean source files contain its records.

code.source:
Need all entered customers → .dt infobase dump.
Need a catalog definition → configuration/source files.
code.output: The format matches what must be preserved.

sections.title: Create without a template or engineering script
paragraphs: In the startup list click Add, create a new infobase, then choose creation without a configuration for development. Name it My training service desk, keep placement on this computer and choose a separate directory. Do not use installed third-party templates. Keep other normal defaults unless the official instructions for your version require otherwise.

An empty infobase has no customers or documents yet. That is expected. The applied track will prepare a small original application; programming lessons gradually define their own objects. Neither Studio nor Windows Sandbox is required here.

sections.title: Formats preserve different things
paragraphs: A .cf file preserves the application configuration, not all entered customer records. An infobase dump .dt transfers infobase state. Definition files and module sources help development and comparison, but do not replace data backup. Choose by the content that must survive.

In your own Designer use Administration → Dump infobase. Choose a new dated .dt filename and wait for completion. A file existing is only the first check. Verify usability by loading it into another demonstrably empty infobase and comparing behavior.

sections.title: Restore without replacing the original
paragraphs: Verify a new target directory before loading.

code.source: Mine → new .dt → new empty Restore check → load there

tables.caption: Step-by-step reasoning
rows: New empty entry and directory verified

sections.title: Restoration must leave the original intact
paragraphs: Close the original, create another empty infobase in a new directory and name it Training service desk — restore check. Start Designer from that verified entry. Load infobase replaces the target contents: cancel if you cannot establish that the target is the new empty copy. Do not experiment on your primary work.

Open the restored copy and repeat the available action. At this early stage compare structure; after entering customers compare codes, names and counts. A successful empty-base check does not prove preservation of future documents. Keep the original and backup separately. Nexus cloud state is not a backup of an external 1C infobase.

sections.title: Check your explanation
paragraphs: I copy only a startup shortcut. It points to storage but does not preserve the data.
I call .cf a full data backup. It preserves configuration; use the infobase .dt dump for state.

selfcheck.prompt: Which file preserves infobase state including entered customers?
selfcheck.feedback: A definition and a location pointer are not data backups.

selfcheck.prompt: Where should a restoration check load .dt?
options: Into a new empty infobase in a verified separate directory
Into any entry with the same title

selfcheck.prompt: Why is an existing .dt not sufficient verification?
selfcheck.feedback: Usability requires a repeatable restoration, not a filename.

selfcheck.prompt: Dump your infobase and restore it into a new empty one. State exactly what can be compared at this stage.
selfcheck.feedback: A new directory is used, original work survives and no claims concern nonexistent data.

practice.title: A new infobase and a separate restored copy
practice.task: Dump your infobase and restore it into a new empty one. State exactly what can be compared at this stage.
practice.environment: Normal local training-edition installation; no business databases or paid services.

steps.title: Create an empty infobase
steps.action: Create without configuration, name it My training service desk, place it on this computer in a new directory and finish the wizard.
steps.why: Separate storage avoids replacing other work.
steps.expected: Your own startup entry points to the chosen directory.
steps.troubleshooting: If shown a third-party template, go back and choose creation without configuration.
steps.before: The official training platform is installed; a new separate infobase directory is available.

steps.title: Open and dump
steps.action: Open configuration. Use Administration → Dump infobase, choose a new .dt and wait for completion. Close your Designer session.
steps.expected: A new .dt exists; the original was not replaced.
steps.troubleshooting: Do not confuse Load with Dump; cancel if uncertain.
steps.before: Your own startup entry points to the chosen directory.

figures.caption: Dump infobase saves state into a new .dt. Do not confuse it with Load below.
figures.alt: Dump infobase saves state into a new .dt. Do not confuse it with Load below.

steps.title: Prepare a check target
steps.action: Create another empty infobase named Training service desk — restore check in another new directory. Verify that entry and its directory before launch.
steps.why: Restoration must target an empty copy.
steps.expected: Primary and check entries are distinguishable by location.
steps.troubleshooting: Matching window titles are insufficient; return to the startup list.
steps.before: A new .dt exists; the original was not replaced.

steps.title: Restore into the check infobase
steps.where: Designer of the verified empty check target
steps.action: Only after verifying the empty target, use Administration → Load infobase, select your .dt and wait. Cancel if the destination is uncertain.
steps.expected: The separate copy is restored; the original is untouched.
steps.troubleshooting: Do not confirm replacement in an unidentified infobase.
steps.before: Primary and check entries are distinguishable by location.

steps.title: Open each in turn
steps.action: Compare available structure in the restored and original infobases one at a time. Note that application records do not exist yet. Keep both directories and the .dt.
steps.expected: Restoration and its actual scope are recorded.
steps.troubleshooting: If different, preserve both and recheck the selected dump; do not overwrite the original.
steps.before: The separate copy is restored; the original is untouched.
